input.statement:
MATCH (a:Airport)-[:IN_COUNTRY]->(:Country {code:'MX'}), (m:Airport {iata:'MEX'})
WHERE a <> m AND NOT (a)-[:HAS_ROUTE]->(m)
MATCH (a)-[:HAS_ROUTE]->(h:Airport)-[:HAS_ROUTE]->(m)
WHERE h <> a
MATCH (h)-[:IN_COUNTRY]->(c:Country)
WITH a, count(DISTINCT h) AS hubs, collect(DISTINCT c.code) AS hub_countries
WHERE hubs >= 2
RETURN a.iata AS airport, hubs, hub_countries ORDER BY airport

content.text:
Four Mexican airports have no direct flight to MEX but would still reach it in two flights if any single hub closed. I took that to mean at least two distinct intermediate hubs, so no one hub is a single point of failure.

| Airport | Distinct hubs | Hub countries |
|---|---|---|
| PBC | 7 | MX, US |
| QRO | 9 | MX, US |
| TLC | 10 | MX, US |
| UPN | 2 | MX, US |

I counted a hub only when the route direction runs airport → hub → MEX. In every case the hubs are in Mexico (MX) or the United States (US).
